subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Water Footprint
description: A fast breakdown of Water Footprint for builders.

hook.text: It takes 10,000 liters of water to make one pair of jeans. Most of that water is used in the supply chain.

buildup.text: The water footprint measures total water consumed across a product's supply chain—from farm to factory.

discovery.text: Water-intensive industries—textiles, agriculture, electronics—face growing risks as water scarcity increases.

twist.text: Water is local. A factory using water in a water-scarce region causes more harm than the same use in a wet region.

climax.text: Companies like Levi's reduced water use by 96% in finishing processes through innovation and redesign.

punchline.text: Water is finite. Supply chains that waste it face a dry future.

quiz.question: How much water does one pair of jeans require?
